newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul shares end lower as profit-taking sets in.
newsitem.headline: Seoul shares end lower as profit-taking sets in.

text.p: Profit-taking set in during Thursday's afternoon session, paring away earlier gains, brokers said.

Brokers said Wednesday's technical rebound was over and the market was headed downwards unless unforeseen good news emerged. "There are no good market factors," said Jay Kwon of Hanhwa Securities. "In this bearish market, it's easy to freeze sentiment."
The composite stock index ended down 5.53 points to a provisional 741.76. Decliners overtook advancers 553 to 341, with 118 unchanged.
Blue chips were mixed. Samsung Electronics fell 2,000 won to 61,000 on profit-taking, while Korea Mobile Telecom gained 10,000 won to 463,000.
Construction shares rose on expectations of large infrastructure projects in 1997. Hanshin Construction rose 130 won to 5,580.
LG Information closed 4,500 won to its limit of 71,800. It was seen losing out against Daewoo Telecom's role as equipment provider to Korea Telecom. Daewoo rose 40 won to 10,000.
The listing of LG Semicon's 10 million new shares on Saturday was a major dampener, brokers said.

The oversupply of shares has become a focus of investor fears. Customer deposits declined to around 2.5 trillion, and new stock supply in November is estimated at more than 1.1 trillion won, broker said.
Margin loans, on the other hand, are at record levels, nearing three trillion won. Between 500-900 billion won worth of the loans will have to be repaid this month, brokers said.
